exposure: Robson's Ten Group Classification System categories (e.g., Group 5: previous LSCS, Group 2: nulliparous >37 weeks, induced)
Indications for Caesarean Section (e.g., previous LSCS, foetal distress, meconium-stained liquor)
outcome: contribution of different Robson's groups to caesarean section rates
most common indications for caesarean section
cohort: The study included 739 pregnant women from a single medical college, 348 of whom underwent caesarean section.
finding: The overall caesarean section rate was 47.09%, with Robson's group 5 (previous LSCS) contributing the most (33.33%), followed by group 2 (nulliparous >37 weeks, induced) at 26.15%.
mod_finding: The study identified previous LSCS as the most common indication for caesarean section and suggested offering TOLAC and encouraging versions to reduce caesarean section rates.
